clue.text: Passing criminal sentence requiring Virginia to be imprisoned

indicators.note: the jumbled word needs another piece held inside it, so it acts as the outer shell
a prisoner is locked inside a cell, so this abbreviation goes within the other letters
something criminal is crooked or bent out of true, so these letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A court hands down an odd sentence that sends someone called Virginia to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like part of the courtroom scene but is the definition: EVANESCENT is the rearranged sentence with VA locked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evanescent fades quickly and soon vanishes, so it is passing or transient.

clue.text: Showing Courage barrel pierced by spike from the bottom

indicators.note: something pierced has another object driven into its middle, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a vat is a large barrel-like vessel

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom upwards turns the word backwards

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A wooden barrel gamely withstands having a spike driven up into it from below.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'from the bottom' means read upwards, so the spike runs backwards before it goes into the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Valiant is an adjective for brave conduct, matching the phrase describing someone displaying bravery.

clue.text: Knock over old tin containing hot snack

indicators.note: knocking something over turns it upside down, which in a down entry reverses the order
containing means holding another piece inside, so one letter sits within the others

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a tin is a can
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily topples an old tin with a hot snack inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Old and tin together are turned over to give NACO, and H goes in before the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served with melted cheese as a snack.

clue.text: Big spender visiting classy bar I tended

indicators.note: a visitor is briefly inside a place, so the answer is lodged within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of classy, then bar, I and the start of tended

explanation.surface: A lavish customer drops in at an upmarket bar where the speaker used to serve drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last two letters of 'classy' to the first two of 'tended'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is someone devoted to luxury and pleasure, so likely to splash out lavishly on indulgence.

clue.text: Grandpa goes once around school field event

indicators.note: going around suggests moving every way about, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly man takes a single lap of the track at a school sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-and-spoon race is a classic sports day contest where children run balancing an egg on a spoon, a novelty event on the field.

clue.text: Pitch article about Zulu jungle resident

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so one word wraps the letter that follows

parts.note: pitch is the black sticky substance also called tar
an is the indefinite article
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newspaper pitches a feature on a Zulu warrior living in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' is not a sales pitch but the black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan is the fictional character raised by apes who lives in the African forest.

clue.text: Not many escaping trap — that's a relief!

indicators.note: trap is slang for the mouth, so words escaping it are being spoken out loud

parts.note: few means not many; said out loud it matches the exclamation

explanation.surface: Only a handful slipped out of the ambush, and the speaker sighs with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is the interjection people utter when tension lifts, expressing relief.

clue.text: K P moist USA nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the preceding letters are in a mad jumble

parts.note: the letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Reads like a shopping note for chemical elements and damp American nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: K is the chemical symbol for this element, from its Latin name kalium.
explanation.definitionFit: K is the chemical symbol for potassium in the periodic table.

clue.text: One raised in surprise when discussing East End intellectual?

parts.note: an intellectual is a highbrow; Cockney speech drops its opening h

explanation.surface: Someone's brows shoot up when a clever East Ender joins the conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney area of London, whose accent drops initial h sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift an eyebrow to show astonishment, so it is a feature raised when startled.

clue.text: EU — for one — backed firm pound

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: The European Union is said to have supported a strong pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' seems to mean supported, but it reverses the two short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations allied for common purpose, and the European Union is an example.

clue.text: Reality TV show runs into huge trouble

parts.note: huge means big

indicators.note: going into something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: bother is trouble

explanation.surface: A reality television programme runs into serious difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes inside the word for trouble, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is a well-known reality series in which housemates are filmed constantly.

clue.text: Threaten to host a bachelor party

indicators.note: a host takes guests inside, so the first word holds the next pieces within it

parts.note: to lour (or lower) is to look threatening, as a dark sky does
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bachelor party' reads as one phrase, but 'party' alone is the definition. Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is the name of a major British political party.

clue.text: Koran has adapted storyline from Genesis

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Koran is said to have reworked a story from the Bible's first book.
explanation.definitionFit: The tale of the great flood and the vessel built to save the animals is told in the biblical book of Genesis.

clue.text: Fabulous place, but the bar's a bit of a dive

definitions.text: Fabulous place, but the bar's a bit of a dive

parts.words: Fabulous place, but the bar's a bit of a dive
parts.note: surface reading: a splendid venue let down by a seedy drinking den; setter's reading: a place from fable, i.e. legend, which sank beneath the sea, so it is somewhere you could dive to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means legendary rather than wonderful, and 'dive' is literal: the lost city sank under the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island said by Plato to have sunk into the ocean, a mythical realm now underwater.

clue.text: Nick unfortunately happened to catch onset of rubella

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so the rearranged word takes a letter inside
something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the word before is put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of rubella

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick was unlucky enough to come down with German measles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a person's name but is the slang verb for arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for arresting someone, which is what the police do when they apprehend a suspect.

clue.text: Leaders of independent, outgoing west African state

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'African state' suggests a country in Africa, but the state is in the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Forebear found in seances tormented

indicators.note: found in means lying within, so the answer sits inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run from the third letter of seances into the start of tormented

explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom one is descended, an earlier family member.

clue.text: Sprinter's first time? Record pace

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter alone of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of sprinter
T is the abbreviation for time
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Asks whether a runner's debut set a record speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record pace' reads as a fast time, but the record is the short disc and pace is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single stride, which can also be called a pace.

clue.text: 11 2 beaten after swapping knight for king

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked about out of shape, so the letters are scrambled
swapping one thing for another means a letter is replaced before the rearranging

parts.note: the answer to 2 Down
N is the chess notation for knight
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Cross-references describe a chess fight where a brave player loses a knight and a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 11 Across, LABOUR. Replace the N in VALIANT with R, giving VALIART, then rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail means hard toil or painful effort, just as labour does; both also mean childbirth.

clue.text: Cream program out of date

parts.note: a date is an appointment
an app is a software program

explanation.surface: Describes an obsolete computer program for removing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of date' wants to mean obsolete; split it as 'out of' plus 'date', where a date is an arranged meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a soothing preparation rubbed on the skin, a type of medicinal cream.

clue.text: Planet starts to need extra purified air

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
an air is a tune or melody

clue.text: Show off apartment housing upper- class knight

clue.text: Explorer's maiden voyage cut by 50%, everyone turned back to Lisbon

parts.note: taken as written; its first half is dropped

clue.text: Get free, completely unlimited Tesco paper

taken as written; its first and last letters go

clue.text: Iron and gold loaded in French port — time for small beverage there

clue.text: Dry, except when crossing river

clue.text: Copper penny: large old, old penny

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' sounds like the coin metal but is slang for a police officer; PLOD, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books, is British slang for the police.

clue.text: One helping to sort out intractable court battles?

definitions.text: One helping to sort out intractable court battles?

parts.words: One helping to sort out intractable court battles?
parts.note: surface reading: a mediator who settles stubborn legal disputes; setter's reading: contests on a tennis court level at six games all in a set, settled by a special deciding game

explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court, not a law court, and the intractable battle is a set locked level.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a tiebreaker is the special deciding game played when a set reaches six games each.
